title: Beatrix and the Veil Revisited
premise: Jude Winterbourne, exiled for a storm they never meant to call, has spent nine years keeping the ledgers of the Gilded Veil, a guild that trades in impossible things while staying invisible to both realms. When a child named Sable arrives speaking the First Tongue—the language that once bound the mortal world and the Veil together—Jude learns the old covenant is collapsing, and every impossible thing the guild ever sold is being called home to pay its debt. Hunted by the magistrates who exiled them and betrayed by the guildmaster who knew all along, Jude must gather the scattered covenant-bearers and reforge the pact at the Well of First Words. In the end Jude chooses justice over pardon: they restore the covenant but refuse the realms' old terms, rewriting it so no one—storm-caller or child—is ever exiled again, at the cost of their own name in both worlds.
about_author: Hazel Oyelaran is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers from port cities before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who keep books, keep secrets, and keep each other.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A quiet night of inventory at the Gilded Veil establishes the guild's strange wares and Jude's careful invisibility. The emotional beat is loneliness disguised as competence—Jude knows every item's price but nothing of belonging.

chapters.title: A Knock in the First Tongue
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A mud-soaked child, Sable, arrives speaking words that make the guild's wares hum in answer. Jude recognizes the language from their exile trial. The beat is fear curdling into reluctant protectiveness as Jude hides the child from the night porter.

chapters.title: What the Guildmaster Knew
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane's POV. Corvane reveals he has been expecting Sable for years—and that the guild's fortune was built on fragments of the broken covenant. The beat is chilling revelation: Jude's sanctuary was always a trap with soft walls.

chapters.title: Storms Remember Their Callers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Magistrates arrive hunting the child; Jude's suppressed storm-magic stirs for the first time in nine years. They flee with Sable through the flooded undercity. The beat is terror and exhilaration—power returning feels like coming home to a burning house.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with new ally Wren, a disgraced mapmaker who charts places that don't exist. Wren agrees to guide them to the first covenant-bearer. The beat is tentative trust: three broken people forming the ragged edge of a family.

chapters.title: Debts Called Home
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Across the land, sold impossibilities vanish—rivers unmake themselves, a city's luck evaporates—as the covenant forecloses. The beat is mounting dread and moral weight: everything the guild traded was stolen from the world's bones.

chapters.title: The Bearer of the Second Word
chapters.summary: Sable's POV (rendered through Jude's translation). The party finds an ancient ferrywoman who tests them with the covenant's second word; Sable, not Jude, answers correctly. The beat is awe and humility—Jude realizes the child is the covenant's true heir, not its cargo.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Corvane sells their route to the magistrates; Wren is captured buying time. Jude faces a choice between rescue and the rendezvous. The beat is fury and heartbreak—justice outside the law demands sacrifice the law would never ask.

chapters.title: The Well of First Words
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the Well, the realms' old terms demand a new exile to seal the covenant—Sable. Jude calls the storm they were exiled for, deliberately this time, shattering the Well's authority. The beat is defiant climax: refusing the bargain, rewriting it aloud in the First Tongue with Sable.

chapters.title: No One Exiled Again
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The new covenant holds; the magistrates' warrant dissolves mid-word. The Gilded Veil reopens under collective stewardship, Wren freed, Corvane bound by his own debts. The beat is quiet resolution—Jude has no name in either realm, but for the first time, a family.
